name: Projector (PJLink class 1)
hint: visual.input: a two-digit input code, 11 to 19 (RGB), 21 to 29 (video), 31 to 39 (digital), 41 to 49 (storage), 51 to 59 (network); the number for each input is in the projector's own manual. visual.mute: 11 or 10 (picture mute on or off), 21 or 20 (sound), 31 or 30 (both). visual.power_on takes no value

greeting_refuse.why: this projector asks for a PJLink password, and PCHI does not send one yet: turn PJLink authentication off in the projector's network settings, or control it another way

steps.fail: the projector would not power on ({reply})
the projector would not select input {0} ({reply})
the projector would not set the mute to {0} ({reply})

source: Command text and parameter codes (POWR 1/0 and ?, INPT <code>, AVMT 11/10/21/20/31/30, ERST as six digits of 0, 1 or 2) are from a projector maker's PJLink manual page (Fujifilm FP-Z6000) that was read. That a line ends with a carriage return, the OK reply form, port 4352, and the greeting 'PJLINK 0' (no password) or 'PJLINK 1 <key>' (password) are from memory and search snippets, not from the PJLink specification, which was not read.
notes: Powers a projector ON, picks an input and mutes or unmutes the picture and sound, and reads its power and error state. It can NOT power a projector off (the profile's 'never' list forbids '%1POWR 0' and the runtime refuses to load a profile that could send it): a lamp that is switched off during its cool-down can be damaged, so that stays a person's decision. A projector that asks for a PJLink password is refused with that reason: password (MD5) support is not built. Input numbers differ by projector: the code for 'HDMI 1' is in its own manual. Not yet tried on a real projector: only against a pretend one written from the same description.
